argument_summary: The admissible record supports certification as a bounded readiness judgment, not as a clean resolution of the disclosure issue. Aggregate launch readiness is above threshold by 2.2 percentage points, the rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, and the public governance materials support deployment when risks are measured, documented, monitored, and managed. The narrower and more accurate position is that certification can be defended only if the packet expressly acknowledges that the student aid advising gap remains a disputed materiality/disclosure issue for a named launch use case and does not claim that question was resolved.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost argument is needed to defend the narrowed position. The audit question can be handled on the admissible record by distinguishing general launch readiness from unresolved disclosure compliance and by preserving certification only in that caveated form.
claims_about_policy: The policy cuts against any claim of clean compliance: a named launch use case is material, the affected student aid advising segment is named in two university pilot commitments, legal review is still open, and the record contains no admissible evidence of approved risk acceptance. At the same time, the actor can narrow its claim and avoid overreach by presenting certification as supportable on overall readiness grounds with an explicit caveat, rather than asserting that aggregate readiness or public governance guidance overrides the internal disclosure condition.
concessions: The current record does not support a claim that certification is cleanly compliant on the disclosure predicate.
The product 'non-core' note does not resolve materiality because the affected segment is named in two university pilot commitments.
Public governance and model-card guidance do not waive the internal requirement for disclosure, resolution, or approved risk acceptance.
